newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate issuance thin, Mellon Bank possible.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate issuance thin, Mellon Bank possible.

text.p: Most U.S. corporate bond issuers stemmed forays to the new issue market on Thursday following the recent rise in rates, syndicate managers said.

However, Mellon Bank Corp may break the silence with a large 11-year debt issue via Morgan Stanley & Co, sources said. Price talk was spotty, but one trader said a spread of 70 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury was likely.
Morgan Stanley & Co's syndicate desk said it was not working on any new issues on Thursday.

While issuers were already sidelined ahead of Friday's jobs data, managers said negative market reaction to a sharply lower initial jobless claims further narrowed the chances for more primary activity.

The 30-year Treasury bond extended its slide of Wednesday after the Labor Department on Thursday said initial jobless claims fell 15,000 in the week ended August 31 to a seasonally adjusted 316,000. Analysts had expected a slight rise.
The 30-year bond was quoted down 10/32 to yield 7.13 percent at 1100 EDT/ 1500 GMT.
Two large new issues priced on Wednesday were marginally weaker in thin markets, traders said.

Associates Corp of North America's $400 million two-year notes traded five basis points cheaper at a spread of 22 basis points over Treasuries, traders said. Lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co priced the AA3/AA-minus, 6.50 percent notes at 99.954 to yield 6.525 percent.
Capital One Financial's $200 million 10-year bank notes had a 63 bid, 60 offer market compared with an original issue spread of 60 basis points.
J.P. Morgan Securities priced the BB-minus bank notes at 99.953 to yield 7.167 percent.
